When the details of the imaged object become much smaller than the certain value defined by the wavelength of the imaging field and parameters of the imaging set-up, the information about any individual detail tends to zero making practically unfeasible inferring object parameters from the measured correlation functions.

articleTitle: Near-Field High-Resolution Imaging Based on Inverse Equivalent Source Methods
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Standard radar imaging methods work commonly with time-domain or spectral domain back-propagation techniques, which are restricted in terms of flexibility and spatial resolution. In this work, we investigate inverse source methods with respect to their imaging capabilities. In an inverse source method, we explicitly solve a linear inverse problem for the given, possibly irregularly distributed measurement samples, and with full probe correction. Moreover, we assume certain a priori knowledge about the location of the equivalent sources on the device under test (DUT). Such a formulation can be set up in form of a radiation problem or in form of a scattering problem, where the sources are rather scattering coefficients than current distributions. Our basic formulation works with time-harmonic high-frequency excitation where, however, several frequencies can be processed in order to combine the results to images with a larger information content.

articleTitle: High-Q states in subwavelength dielectric resonators forming in strong mode coupling regime
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Summary form only given. Resonator is one of the main component of almost any optoelectronic and photonic device. Quality (Q) factor is the most important characteristic of the resonator showing its ability to amplify the external electromagnetic field. There are a lot of types of optical resonator, e.g., photonic crystal cavities, Fabry-Perot resonators, whispering gallery mode resonator and many others. The high record values of Q factor today rich giant values up 1010. However, decrease of the size of any named above resonators results in exponential drop of their Q factor. When the size of the resonator is comparable with vacuum wavelength (the case of the lower Mie-resonance), the value of Q-factors is about 10-20, which is not enough for many practical applications. Therefore, the quest for compact photonic systems makes a new query for small high-Q resonators, using fundamentally new principles of light trapping. In this work we reveal new mechanism of efficient light trapping in subwavelength resonators based on strong coupling between its modes [1,2]. We demonstrate that strong mode coupling results in resonances with high quality factors, which are related to the physics of bound states in the continuum when the radiative losses are almost suppressed due to the Friedrich-Wintgen scenario of destructive interference (Fig. 1). We explain the physics of these states in terms of multipole decomposition, and show that their appearance is accompanied by a drastic change in the far-field radiation pattern. We reveal a fundamental link between the formation of the high quality resonances and peculiarities of the Fano parameter in the scattering cross-section spectra. Our theoretical findings are confirmed by microwave experiments for the scattering of high-index cylindrical resonators with a tunable aspect ratio.

articleTitle: Massively Parallel Multiphysics Solver for Simulating Large-Scale Antenna Array and Other 3-D Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, a massively parallel multiphysics solver, based on an in-house massively parallel computing scheme for supercomputing, is developed for simulating large-scale antenna array and other 3-D structures, with domain decomposition method (DDM) also employed. During our simulation, frequency-domain electromagnetic fields are computed at first by solving the Helmholtz equation, and then the dissipated power is characterized, which is the heat source in the thermal co-simulation. New temperature profile can be obtained at the end of each iteration step, and they can be used to update all temperature-dependent parameters of the structure. This process is repeated until the temperature difference converge is achieved with a preset tolerance. The developed multiphysics solver is validated by comparing the results with that of commercial software. In particular, its speedup, scalability and efficiency are tested and examined.

articleTitle: On Linear and Sesquilinear Boundary Conditions in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The most general form of linear boundary conditions in electromagnetics can be expressed in terms of two scalar-valued equations of the form f1(E,H)=0$ and f2(E,H)=0, where f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> are two bilinear functions, each defined by two vector quantities.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of passively-fed dipole arrays with improved specific absorption rate efficiency and reduced loading effects for ultra-high field MRI
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Summary form only given. MRI at Ultrahigh Field (UHF) is complicated by interferences that occur in the transmit field (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) as a result of the relatively short wavelength of the RF transmit field compared to the dimensions of the imaging region [1], [2]. These interferences produce areas of spatially dependent image contrasts. In order to mitigate the inhomogeneous transmit field, multichannel transmit array systems have been developed. In such a system it is possible to independently control the amplitude and/or phase of each individual element, as well as to apply different RF pulses to each channel. As an element in multichannel array systems dipole antenna has been proposed [3, 4]. The design philosophy is that instead of designing high quality factor resonant structures, rather dipole antennas are used where the radiative field component is dominant compared to the reactive field component. The main advantages of the dipole-type antennas over conventional loop-coil resonators include more symmetric excitation patterns, which allows more simple B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> shimming, and a slightly higher transmit efficiency (defined as B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> per square root maximum SAR) for organs deep in the body [3, 4]. For all of the dipole geometries described in the literature the element is directly-fed via a partially- or fully balanced lumped matching element network consisting of capacitors and/or inductors. However, it is also possible to feed dipole elements passively, i.e. via inductive and capacitive coupling from a passive structure which is coupled to the dipole [5, 6]. A passively-fed antenna consists of a short feeding dipole (printed on one side of a dielectric substrate) which is connected to the coaxial cable and matching circuit. The main radiating element is printed on the other side of the substrate. In this work, we evaluate experimentally and in simulations the passive-feeding approach for different dipole antenna elements (straight, meander, snake) used as array elements for body imaging and brain imaging at 7T. To illustrate the performance of the passively fed antenna element in an eight-channel transmit head/body array, we compared its simulated performance (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> per unit input power, local SAR, and B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> per maximum local SAR) to the performance of a directly fed dipole antenna element with the same length. Images of prostate and brain have been obtained in-vivo in healthy volunteers.

articleTitle: Field Quantization in Arbitrarily-Shaped Metal Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the last few decades, plasmon nanoparticles (NP) have been proposed as a suitable platform to control and enhance the light-matter interaction. Nowadays, modern technologies are pushing this interaction to the extreme: single quantum emitters can be isolated, few-nanometer particles can be fabricated, single-photon state can be measured. For a complete analysis of the coupling phenomena involving plasmon nanoparticles, a proper quantum description is needed.

articleTitle: Efficient modeling of modulated metasurface antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Modulated metasurface (MTS) antennas [1] can provide high to very-high gains, purely polarized radiation and shaped beams, while preserving a low-profile and low-weight. This class of antenna radiates gradually the power carried by a surface-wave (SW), due to the SW interaction with a modulated impedance plane consisting of a sub-wavelength textured surface. The characteristics of modulated MTS have drawn a lot of attention, and present them as a good alternative to more conventional high-gain structures, such as reflector or lens antennas and antenna arrays. Although reflectors and lenses offer an excellent performance, they are bulky and, sometimes, it is not easy to integrate them in moving platforms. Regarding antenna arrays, one has to distribute the signal to each antenna element with feeding networks, which adds additional losses. In turn, the main disadvantages of MTS antennas are their typically narrow bandwidth and the additional developments required to obtain multi-beam architectures [2].

articleTitle: Importance of the Dispersion Principles in System Design
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Many of the components of Electrical engineering have been developed primarily to deal with the phenomenon of dispersion. Dispersion is a fact of life and it states that the phase/group velocity of a waveform is a function of its frequency. In optics this is reflected as the rainbow in the sky where the different components of white light separates out as it traverses through a dielectric medium namely the rain drop which disperses the various components into several colors as each color has a different velocity of propagation. In short even when propagating in free space since the phase velocity associated with each frequency is different there develops naturally a distortion phenomenon because of the variation of the phase velocity with frequency. In electrical engineering it is more subtle. It happens both in audio and radio frequency signals. Therefore to prevent the distortion of a transmitted message recourse is taken to modulation. There will be no modulation schemes if there is no dispersion! Modulation essentially takes a band of signals and generally translates them to a much higher frequency so that now the effective bandwidth of the same signal will be much smaller than what it would be in its base band. Since, now the translated frequencies through modulation has now effectively a smaller band of frequencies the distortion in that smaller band will be small and hence distortion will be absent for all practical purposes.

articleTitle: A Stabilized Solution of Time-Domain Combined Field Integral Equation using Associated Laguerre Functions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The time domain integral equation (TDIE) using associated Laguerre functions [1] is one of the promising transient and broadband computational electromagnetic methods. It is a marching-on-in-degree (MOD) method for solving various electromagnetic compatibility and electromagnetic interference (EMC & EMI) problems. Over the past decades, the instability of time-domain integral equation remains one of the main obstacles to improve the quality of the TDIE solutions. The MOD method adopts the associated Laguerre functions as temporal basis functions. As the associated Laguerre polynomials decays exponentially in time, the MOD scheme is immune to the late-time unstable behavior of marching-on-in-time methods (MOT). Although the MOD solver is assumed to be stable, there still exists an instabilty when the TDIE-MOD scheme marches on to very high degree of the Laguerre polynomials [2]. The main reason is that MOD iterates with respect to the polynomial degrees rather than the time steps. The instability related to the MOD solution of time-domain magnetic field integral equation (TD-MFIE-MOD) and time-domain electric integral equation (TD-EFIE-MOD) are eliminated by a Filon-type quadrature for associated Laguerre polynomials, and a novel Filon-type radial integration method for oscillatory quadrature on triangular patches, which are proposed in [2], [3]. On the other hand, the exact temporal Galerkin testing procedure in the MOD solution is affected by an unbounded initial value of the transient current density, which allows numerical errors to accumulate and affect the ultimate stability. Therefore, a sequential constraint term needs to be added without destroying the causality of the MOD method.

articleTitle: On the design of broadband resonant cavity antennas with feeds suitable for integration with millimeter-wave transceiver chips
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the resonant cavity antenna's (RCA) integration capability with the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) transceiver chips. A broadband RCA fed by a probe-fed microstrip patch, which is readily integrated with transceiver chips, is designed at 60 GHz. It exhibits a peak broadside gain of 19 dBi with a VSWR 2:1 bandwidth ranging from 57 GHz to beyond 70 GHz. Radiation performance of the RCA fed by a traditional waveguide aperture is also presented to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed RCA in mm-wave practical applications.

articleTitle: On the Existence of Terahertz Plasmons in Two-dimensional Semiconductor Heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Plasmons existing along a semiconductor heterostructure found in a high electron mobility transistor are studied. With the help of the electronic properties of group III-V semiconductor materials, a multilayer structure is described using an equivalent transmission line network. The existence of surface waves is investigated using the transverse resonance method, and it is established that the complex conductivity of the two-dimensional electron gas with a negative imaginary part yields surface plasmons in the terahertz frequency domain.

articleTitle: Application of the discrete dipole approximation in microwave breast imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this work, we propose the two-dimensional discrete dipole approximation (2D DDA) to calculate the electric field distributions in the microwave imaging system. The motive is to develop a significantly fast reconstruction algorithm. To accomplish this, the 2D DDA on a uniform grid in the forward model zone is used, which enables computational times be significantly reduced compared to common algorithms.

articleTitle: Maser radiation in the laboratory and space plasmas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An electron beam driven cyclotron maser emission is responsible for the earth's auroral kilometric radiation (AKR) and for intense circularly polarized radiation emitted from the auroral regions of magnetized planets. The sun and certain types of stars such as UV Ceti and CU Virginus also radiate intense circularly polarized radiation by a cyclotron maser process. These emissions are attributed to energetic electrons moving into convergent magnetic fields that are typically found in association with dipole like planetary magnetospheres e.g. the auroral region of magnetized planets. It is found that magnetic compression leads to the formation of a velocity distribution having a horseshoe shape or crescent shape as a result of conservation of the electron magnetic moment. Intense maser radiation from Blazar jets can also be described by a similar model. In the case of a Blazar jet a collisionless shock wave is responsible for the energizing the electrons which form a horseshoe like distribution in a convergent magnetic field. We will discuss recent developments in the theory and simulation of the instability including addressing, the origin of the accelerated electrons, radiation escape avoiding strong absorption at the second harmonic, and relate these to satellite observations. Measurements of the conversion efficiency, mode and spectral content are in close agreement with the predictions of numerical simulations undertaken using a particle-in-cell code and also with satellite observations confirming the horseshoe maser as an important emission mechanism in geophysical and astrophysical plasmas.

articleTitle: Stimulated Fore-wake Excitations from Moving Charged Objects in the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: When a charged object moves in a plasma it can create a wake structure behind it consisting of electrostatic or electromagnetic waves in a manner analogous to wakes created by boats or marine animals moving in water. However, when the boat speed exceeds a critical velocity, like the phase speed of the surface water waves, it can excite nonlinear structures in the form of solitons or shocks that move away from it in the forward direction. Such fore-wake excitations have been predicted and widely studied in hydrodynamics [1], [2]; precursor solitons have also been observed in laboratory experiments of models ships being towed in shallow water channels [3]. In principle, such a phenomenon should also take place in a plasma when the speed of the charged object exceeds the phase speed of a typical collective mode of the plasma such as the ion acoustic speed or the magneto-sonic speed. Fore-wake excitations have received very little attention in plasma physics although the conditions for such excitations exist naturally in many space plasma situations, e.g. the interaction of the supersonic solar wind component with the earth or moon, the fast streaming of space craft or charged debris objects interacting with the plasma in the ionosphere etc. Recently a proof-of-principle laboratory experiment observed the excitation of upstreaming dust acoustic solitons when a dusty plasma was made to flow supersonically over a stationary electrostatic potential hill [4]. The experimental results were well validated by model calculations based on a forced Korteweg-de Vries (fKdV) equation [4] as well as fluid and molecular dynamic simulations [5]. These precursor structures can be usefully exploited for Space Situational Awareness (SSA) purposes as was suggested in [6] and served as a major motivation for the investigations in [4], [5]. The basic idea is that the multiple emissions of solitons (ion acoustic ones in this case) can create a cloud of plasma irregularity that may be easily detectable from the earth and act as a tracking aid for the debris. However these electrostatic structures can be quite short lived due to strong Landau damping in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) region and electromagnetic nonlinear structures might provide a better alternative by creating longer life time and larger spatial extent irregularity clouds. In this presentation, after a brief review of past work on electrostatic excitations, we will discuss the stimulated excitation of electromagnetic waves. Treating the moving charged object as a current source we have developed an appropriate theoretical framework to study the excitation of electromagnetic waves like magneto-sonic waves, shear Alfven waves etc. A nonlinear formulation, based on the reductive perturbation technique, provides an equation analogous to the fKdV for the study of electromagnetic emissions. We use analytic and numerical solutions of this equation to discuss the features of magneto-sonic solitons and magneto-sonic shocks in the LEO region and delineate the parametric regimes and conditions for their excitation. The results are further extended using a full set of two fluid equations for ionospheric conditions and obtaining numerical solutions under various conditions. We also discuss the feasibility of exciting and detecting such structures in a laboratory setup.

articleTitle: Hopf solutions of Maxwell equations: analysis and simulation by FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution studies a particular solution of Maxwell wave equations known as Hopfions by making use of the well-known Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. Hopfions are a family of solutions, in which the field lines are closed, forming different knot topologies that are preserved during its time evolution. These solutions have been studied in different analytical ways (e.g. [1]), but which to the best of our knowledge they have never been simulated before. Their simulation can be of interest because they are demonstrated to exist, not from purely analytical arguments, but from the direct numerical resolutions of the Maxwell's curl equations. This numerical solution would ease the study of how these fields could interact with other structures made of different materials, with other Hopfions, and on how they could be possibly be generated with antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Exceptional Points of Degeneracy induced in Uniform and Periodic Coupled Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Exceptional points of degeneracy (EPDs) are points in parameters space of a waveguide system where two or more eigenmode coalesce into a single degenerate eigenmode. EPDs are obtained in electromagnetic structures through proper engineering to one or more system parameters such as dielectric constant, structural dimensions, coupling coefficients, etc. At EPD, the matrix describing the evolution of the system (i.e. the system matrix in uniform waveguides or the transmission matrix in periodic waveguides) is defective which means it is either similar to a Jordan matrix or to a matrix containing a Jordan block. Such condition is achieved either through the involvement of gain and loss in parity-time (PT-) symmetric structures, or via periodicity in the system, for example. Moreover, uniform coupled waveguide can exhibit EPDs in their dispersion diagram by properly coupling evanescent modes to propagating modes, without the need to resort to loss and/or gain.

articleTitle: Dual- and Wide-Band Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized CPW-Fed Slot Antenna with a T-shaped Ground Stub
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A novel dual- and wide-band dual-sense circularly polarized (CP) slot antenna is proposed in this paper. A T-shaped stub is embedded in the asymmetrical ground plane to enhance the bandwidth. By parametric studying, the mechanism of band improvement and circular polarization are presented. The size of the proposed antenna is 40×40×1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (0.48×0.48×0.02λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). The full-wave simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth is 0.30GHz (1.65-1.95GHz) and 4.22GHz (2.43-6.65GHz). The axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) is 0.61GHz (1.41-2.02GHz) and 4.22GHz (2.63-6.85GHz). A prototype of proposed antenna is fabricated and measured, and the measurement agrees well with the simulation, which proves an excellent circularly polarized property.

articleTitle: Study on Fast Algorithms in Multiphysics Thorax Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work studies the feasibility of jointly applying electrical impedance, microwave, and low-frequency ultrasound to monitor the fluids and gas content in human thorax.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Angular Momentum and Angular Power Flux Density in Complex Electromagnetic Environments
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Recently, there has renewed and growing interest in the characterization of spin (SAM) and orbital (OAM) angular momentum (OAM) of electromagnetic waves, with a view to potential applications in increasing capacity of wireless communication systems. Both the generation and the accurate detection and evaluation of OAM in reference and real-life electromagnetic environments is posing new challenges.

articleTitle: Kinetic Physics of Dipolarization Fronts: Theory, Simulation, Laboratory Experiments and in situ Observations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Dipolarization fronts (DFs) are fast Earthward propagating plasma structures with spatial gradients (in the frame moving with the front) of the order of the ion gyroradius or smaller. Broadband, mostly electrostatic, wavepower is observed at the front and complex nonlinear electromagnetic waves behind the front. DFs are thought to be formed in the magnetotail due to magnetic reconnection that depletes a flux-tube of plasma. This depleted flux-tube is buoyant and thus rushes towards the Earth. DFs are important for transporting particles and energy from the magnetotail into the inner magnetosphere.

articleTitle: A Circularly-Polarized Beam-shaped Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly-polarized beam-shaped antenna has been proposed. The phase delayed power divider is used as the feeding network of the antenna. By the method of simulation, the design indicates the antenna obtains low reflection coefficient, and generates beam which swicthes off about 15 degrees. The gain of the antenna is about 10dB and the antenna covers 35° in the H-plane, 120° in the E-plane with the gain greater than 5dB beam width. The antenna has been used as a dual-antennas communication system to achieve omnidirectional beam. It can be widely applied to communication and measurement systems.

articleTitle: An Overview of the EDA-Workshop “Radar Signatures & EM Benchmarks”
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Computational Electromagnetics (CEM) has been an important planning tool for radar systems as well as antenna development and military aircraft design for many decades. A large variety of electromagnetic (EM) modelling tools has been developed and is available as both commercial software suites and highly specialized scientific codes that are able to handle extremely complex tasks of EM simulation. With the growing relevance of automotive radar and 5G systems during the last few years, CEM methods have gained an even higher level of significance. As an example, automotive radars for autonomous driving are sometimes required to be tested over more than one million kilometers, which in many cases is hardly feasible in real experiments. In the context of military aircraft, ships, or other vehicles, the radar cross section (RCS) is a crucial figure, which, during the planning stage, can be obtained only in simulations.

articleTitle: Novel Post-Processing Technique In Free Space Transmission Loss Measurement Of Multi-Layer Dielectric Material Parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Novel post-processing technique of wideband free space transmission loss only measurement of multi-layer dielectric material parameters is introduced. This new technique significantly improves the accuracy of material parameters extracted from measured data that contain very high level of quasi-random measurement errors.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of Nonlinear Metamaterial Rod
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We consider propagation of leaky and surface TE waves in the rod filled with nonlinear metamaterial medium. The physical setting is reduced to a transmission eigenvalue problem for an ordinary differential equation. The eigenvalues of the problem are the wave propagation constants. For the numerical solution, a method is proposed based on solving an auxiliary Cauchy problem (a version of the shooting method). As a result of comprehensive numerical modeling, new propagation regimes are discovered.

articleTitle: Efficient Matrix Filling for a Volume-Surface Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An efficient hybrid method is presented to solve the electromagnetic (EM) scattering from complex thin-layer composite targets. This hybrid method is the combination of volume-surface integral equation (VSIE) and equivalent dipole-moment (EDM). In this VSIE, the Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis functions are used to expanded the surface currents on perfect electric conductor (PEC), and the simplified prism vector (SPV) basis functions are utilized to approximate the volume currents in dielectric volume. In EDM, the SPV basis-based dipole model is presented for thin dielectric volume, and the RWG basis-based dipole model is applied for PEC. The presented model improves the calculating efficiency of numerical integration part within the threshold for thin dielectric in comparison with the widely used the Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis-based dipole model. Besides, the EDM significantly accelerates the filling of impedance matrix elements by avoiding dual or triple integration. Furthermore, in this hybrid method, the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is utilized to accelerate the iterations. Numerical results are shown to illustrate the efficiency and accuracy of the presented method.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis of finite arrays with aperiodical element-wise materials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The efficient and precise analysis of large finite periodic arrays in the scope of the nanotechnology is a current challenge in computational electromagnetics. SlotFFT techniques [1]-[2] have proven to efficiently perform the analysis of this kind of problems. It is a transparent method which maintains the precision of the surface-integral equation-method of moments (SIE-MoM) framework [3]-[4] but reducing the cost of the matrix-vector product (MVP) from O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) to O(nMlog(M)), where n is the number of unknowns of the element, M the number of elements, and N=nM.

articleTitle: Simulation and Validation of a Computer-Aided Design Mobile Phone Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The specific absorption rate (SAR) compliance of wireless communication devices, such as mobile phones, is currently assessed by performing numerous measurements using a standard dosimetric test facility [1]. Considering the number of communication systems embedded in a mobile phone and frequency bands of operation (2G at 900 MHz and 1800 MHz, 3G at 2100 MHz, 4G at 700 MHz and 2600 MHz, WiFi at 2400 MHz) and use configurations (device operated at the ear or body-worn), the standardized SAR measurement procedure proves to be time-consuming and costly. To aid with the development of the computer-aided design (CAD) of such devices, the dual-logo IEC/IEEE 62704-3-2017 SAR pre-compliance standard, which relies on finite difference time domain (FDTD)-based computational tools, has been elaborated [2].

articleTitle: Expedited EM-Driven Optimization of Antenna Structures Using Gradient Search with Jacobian Change and Design Relocation Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Design of modern antenna structures heavily exploits full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulation tools. It is a practical necessity that results from unavailability or unreliability of other evaluation methods. EM-based adjustment of geometry parameter values aiming at improvement of electrical and field characteristics of the antenna at hand (also referred to as design closure) is of growing importance, especially in the case of topologically complex structures. When coupled with numerical optimization algorithms, the process can be automated but its bottleneck is a high computational cost. In this paper, the expedited version of a gradient search algorithm with numerical derivatives is proposed. Two major acceleration mechanisms are involved, a procedure for antenna sensitivity change monitoring as well as omission of finite-differentiation-based Jacobian updates for the parameters with respect to which the design relocation between the algorithm iterations is sufficiently small. Both methods allow us to greatly reduce the need for finite differentiation as a mean for estimating antenna gradients thus leading to considerable reduction of the computational cost of the optimization process (in the excess of 60 percent) while ensuring excellent reliability and repeatability, both measured using statistics over multiple algorithm runs with random initial designs. Comprehensive numerical experiments indicate superiority of the proposed approach over the reference trust-region gradient search algorithm as well as its several accelerated versions, recently reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Tear and Interconnect Domain Decomposition Analysis of Piecewise Penetrable Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Recent advances in nanotechnology have allowed to exploit the capability of the field of plasmonics to confine electromagnetic subwavelength radiation, enhancement, and spatio-temporal control of light and electron beams in the vicinity of metal/dielectric interfaces (in particular in, metallic nanoparticles), with a large amount of cutting-edge applications on several fields, including medicine [1], nanoscale light management, deep-subwavelength optical microscopy, nanoscale communications or quantum optics. However, there are two particularly directions which are truly interesting for all of them, surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) [2] and the use of electron beam excitations to induce light emission and improve spatial resolution, wavelength-resolved cathodoluminescence (CL) light emission and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) [3].

articleTitle: Stable Discretization of Time-Domain Solvers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Applications at the intersection of quantum and EM physics are becoming more prevalent in the engineering community. Interestingly, many of these applications require solving purely classical EM problems to characterize the most important dynamics of the system. As a result, computational electromagnetics (CEM) can play a vital role in this new area. However, the classical problems that typically need to be solved are the broadband analysis of near-field scattering problems in complicated regions with multiscale and/or subwavelength features. Recently, potential-based time domain integral equations (TDIEs) have been investigated to solve these traditionally challenging CEM problems [1], [2]. However, for these methods to be applicable, they must be robustly stable when analyzing complicated geometries over broad bandwidths.

articleTitle: A quantitative Evaluation for Radar Grid Map Construction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, a quantitative evaluation of the quality of different radar grid map algorithms is performed. Two evaluation indices are proposed as the means to describe the quality of the map. The proposed indices are used to evaluate two types of grid maps, which are built by standard occupancy grid mapping algorithm and by adaptive resolution grid mapping algorithm, respectively. To validate the effectiveness of the evaluation, both numerical simulations and experiments are shown.

articleTitle: Application of Non-singular Laplacian Representations to Analytic Evaluation of 6-dimensional Integrals of the Kernel of Volumetric Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We consider the method of evaluating matrix elements of electromagnetic volume integral equations with the help of suitably constructed Laplacian-type representations of singular kernels (Green functions) appearing in electromagnetic volume and surface integral equations. The method consists of representing the singular kernels (Green functions) in terms of a generalized Laplacian operator acting on some auxiliary functions. Such a representations allow us, by using Gauss divergence theorem, to convert volumetric and surface integrals representing matrix elements to integrals always involving only non-singular integrands. The task of of finding particular Laplacian representation of different kernels amounts to solving appropriate ordinary or partial inhomogeneous differential equations. We apply the Laplacian method to analytic evaluation of matrix elements of the volume integral equation by employing two different Laplacian representations of the integral equation kernels. The first representation allows us to reduce 6-dimensional volume integrals over tetrahedra to 2-dimensional surface integrals over tetrahedra faces. The second representation is subsequently used reducing surface integrals over tetrahedra faces to pairs of of 1-dimensional line integrals over tetrahedra edges. We also derive analytic expressions for the resulting line integrals given in terms of elementary functions.

articleTitle: Highly Directive Leaky-Wave Antennas Based on PT-Symmetric Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present here parity-time (PT)-symmetric metasurfaces that effectively form an artificial channel (or metachannel) with exotic zero-or low-index characteristics. We show that this PT-synthetic metachannel locked at the coherent perfect absorber-laser (CPAL) point can support an almost nonattenuated fast-wave propagation, thus resulting in a highly directive radiation leakage. Further, the directive beam can be steered from broadside to end-fire by varying the gain-loss parameter (or non-Hermiticity) of the PT system.

articleTitle: Recent advances in our understanding of the Earth's Radiation Belts
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Earth's radiation belts were discovered by James van Allen more than fifty years ago and are a home to a plethora of fascinating processes ranging from low energy cold plasma to relativistic and ultra-relativistic particle populations. The traditional morphological picture of the radiation belts is that of an outer belt comprising mostly of electrons and an inner belt comprising mostly of protons with a so-called slot region separating the two. The inner belt is somewhat stable, while the outer radiation belt is very dynamical and shows variability in energetic electron populations over a wide range of energies, intensities, and time scales ranging from minutes, days and even years. This variability is due to dynamical processes of energization and loss with a variety of plasma waves playing an important and crucial role. The traditional picture has recently been challenged with new observations coming from the twin spacecraft mission, Van Allen Probes launched in the fall of 2012, which carries a comprehensive suite of instruments that measure particles and plasma waves. In more than 5 years of observations Van Allen Probes has advanced our understanding of fundamental questions regarding the acceleration and loss of outer Van Allen belt electron population. Van Allen Probes observations have also revealed new phenomena such as the “electron Storage ring”, and the “impenetrable barrier”. This article reviews electron dynamics in the Van Allen belts focusing on van Allen Probes observations and discuss exciting new ways of advancing radiation belt science with CubeSats and CubeSat constellations.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness of Cementitious Composites under Stochastic Excitation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The shielding effectiveness (SE) of materials strongly depends on the exciting field characteristics, polarization, angle of incidence, wave impedance. In real life situations building walls are excited in a random way, making this very similar to what happens inside an electromagnetic reverberation chamber (RC). The paper describes how to measure the SE inside an RC to replicate this real life situation. In particular, cementitious composites are characterized because directly useful for the construction of building walls. The method is based on the using of a nested chamber where the sample is inserted, located inside a larger one to randomly excite the sample. Results are presented for different concentration of concrete filling materials.

articleTitle: Application of the Characteristic Basis Function Method Using Geometrically Optimized Function Sets
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We present in this work an efficient strategy for the generation of macro-basis functions based on the location of the sources, the observation points or directions and the geometrical features of the scenario. A ray-tracing processing calculates the position of a number of critical points on the surface, which are subsequently used to determine the optimal number of macro-basis functions for each block. A representative test case is included in order to validate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Design and Numerical Characterization of a Realistic Plasma Dipole
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This work presents the numerical results for a plasma dipole antenna that exploits plasma technology to generate and receive electromagnetic fields. Two models have been considered, namely an ideal plasma dipole, and a realistic plasma dipole. The latter comprises part of the plasma generation equipment (e.g. metal terminations, inductors). The realistic plasma dipole was realized in practice and tested for the plasma density. Moreover, a preliminary test by means of a vector network analyzer with the plasma turned off was undertaken to verify the accuracy of the simulation models. Both the models can achieve good antenna performances. However, a downshift in the operational frequency can be observed when a more realistic design is considered. All the simulated results have been obtained through full-wave numerical simulations in CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of the Conductivity Profile of the Human Head by a Non-Invasive Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Accurate noninvasive monitoring and diagnostic of the functional activity in the brain is highly important for many brain diseases like: Parkinson and Epilepsy. Electroencephalography is the single brain monitoring technique that is noninvasive, portable, passive, with high temporal resolution, and gives a direct measurement of the brain electrical potential distribution. The main disadvantage of the electroencephalography is its low spatial resolution. For diagnosis of brain-related diseases, recording brain activity with both high temporal and spatial resolution is crucial for the localization of confined brain activations and the study of brain mechanism functionality. A new cortical potential imaging (CPI) method gives an accurate estimation of the brain electrical potential map on the cortex surface [1].

articleTitle: Radiation of Electromagnetic Waves from a Nonsymmetric Antenna Located on the Surface of an Open Gyrotropic Cylindrical Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Radiation characteristics of an antenna with the nonsymmetric current specified on the surface of an open gyrotropic cylindrical waveguide is studied. As the filling medium of the waveguide, a cold magnetoplasma is considered. The radiation pattern of such a source is calculated using an approach based on an expansion of the total field in terms of the discrete- and continuous-spectrum waves of the waveguide. Conditions are found under which the presence of a gyrotropic guiding structure significantly affects the radiation pattern of the antenna.

articleTitle: Imaging the interior of small Solar bodies: towards a quantitative approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Comets and asteroids, the small bodies of the Solar system, contain unique keys to understand the Early Solar System the posterior evolution of which is still poorly known. Our knowledge of the internal structure of comets and asteroids is, unfortunately, so far only indirect and is based on remote sensing observations of their surfaces and on theoretical modelling of their formation and evolution [1].

articleTitle: Plenary Lectures
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the plenary presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Electrostatic and thermal control of Dyakonov–Tamm waves guided by a graphene-coated structurally chiral medium
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The canonical problem for the propagation of a Dyakonov-Tamm Wave (DTW) guided by the surface of a structurally chiral medium coated by a graphene monolayer was numerically solved. The phase speed and propagation distance of the DTW propagating along a fixed direction in the graphene plane were computed in relation to the temperature and an external electrostatic field, both affecting the conductivity of graphene. At least one DTW propagates in any propagation direction, whereas two DTWs propagate in some limited ranges of directions. The phase speed is practically independent of the temperature and the electrostatic field. On the contrary, the propagation distance is noticeably affected by both parameters.

articleTitle: Basins of Attraction in Asymmetric Photonic Couplers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Two nonlinear RF photonic waveguides, one active and one lossy, are paired in a coupler setup. The stability of the configuration is investigated for various degrees of asymmetry between gain and loss, while the role of distance between the two components is examined. The enhancing influence of the gain saturation on system's stability and bistability is identified, while the basins of attraction for each fixed point are determined. The reported results unveil a wealth of dynamical features which are essential in various applications like non-reciprocal propagation, ultra-sensitive microwave sensing and tunable power teleportation.

articleTitle: Analytical Regularization Method for Wave Diffraction by Toroidal Bodies and Screens of Revolution
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The subject herein is a modeling of wave diffraction by axially symmetrical toroidal obstacles: infinitely thin screens and smooth bodies. The approach is based on a further development of Analytical Regularization Method as a new mathematically rigorous and numerically efficient tool for simulation of Dirichlet boundary value problem of wave diffractions by axially symmetrical toroidal obstacles - see Fig. 1. Our previous publications [1]-[5] are devoted to the similar problems, but for axially symmetrical bowl shaped obstacles, when the obstacles have common points with the axis of symmetry. The subject of this presentation is our new mathematically rigorous and numerically efficient modeling of wave diffractions by axially symmetrical toroidal obstacles - see Fig. 1. Our approach has some similarity with methods [2]-[4], but requires essential rearrangement due to the qualitative difference of the obstacles topology. For this purpose, we use Analytical Regularization of integral operators of corresponding functional classic equations of the first kind

articleTitle: A Study on Impact of Component and Module-Level Replacement on Electromagnetic Compatibility Qualification in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Impact of component and module-level replacement on electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) qualification in nuclear power plants is studied in this paper. Recently component or module of instrument and control (I&C) devices is replace for many reason such as unavailability of the existing component and upgrading from analog to digital. Nevertheless, it is difficult to find testing practice and acceptance criteria for the situation but there is an impractical aspect to test the whole system as the initial EMC verification. Technical reports and industrial standards for the practical EMC qualification of component or module-level replacement are investigated. The prototype digital I&C cabinet in Korea nuclear power plant is analyzed to evaluate the EMC characteristic and especially the modeling and EM simulation of POSAFE-Q programmable logic controller with card type module configuration change is performed.

articleTitle: Properties of Glide Symmetric Structures: a Multimodal Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Glide symmetry is a higher order symmetry of periodic structures whose unit cell is invariant under a translation and a mirror reflection, as in Fig. 1(a). Recent studies show that glide symmetry provides interesting characteristics, such as reduced dispersion and wider stop bands which have led to numerous applications in different areas of electromagnetics: ultra-wideband flat metalenses, electromagnetic bandgaps, metamaterial-based microwave circuits [1].

articleTitle: Evaluation of Potential and Impedance Integrals in Case of Singular Bases Along Axially Symmetric Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In the paper singularity cancellation method is considered for precise and efficient evaluation of the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> integration of impedance integrals when using singular basis functions in case of axially symmetric metallic antennas. Several variable transforms are proposed for singularity cancellation. The efficiency of these transforms is analyzed on several examples for various angles between edges and for different positions of the field point.

articleTitle: Overview of plasma wave studies using the Basic Plasma Science Facility
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The Basic Plasma Science Facility (BaPSF) at UCLA is a US national user facility for studies of fundamental processes in magnetized plasmas. The centerpiece of the facility is the Large Plasma Device (LAPD), a 20m long, magnetized linear plasma device<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. This LAPD has been utilized to study a number of fundamental processes, including: collisionless shocks<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, dispersion and damping of kinetic and inertial Alfvén waves<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, compressional Alfvén waves for ion-cyclotron range of frequencies heating<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, flux ropes and magnetic rcconnection<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>, three-wave interactions and parametric instabilities of Alfvén waves<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>, turbulence and transport<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> and interactions of energetic ions and electrons with plasma waves<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>. A brief overview of research using the facility will be given, followed by a more detailed discussion of two recent studies of the physics of Alfvén waves. Recent experiments have resulted in the first laboratory observation of the parametric instability of shear Alfvén waves<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>. Shear waves with sufficiently high and above a threshold wave amplitude are observed to decay into co-propagating daughter waves; one a shear Alfvén wave and the other a low-frequency quasimode. The observed process is similar to the modulational decay instability.

articleTitle: Efficient Electromagnetic Modeling of On-Chip Interconnects with a Hybrid 2D-3D Differential Surface Admittance Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Full-wave electromagnetic simulation is a crucial yet challenging step in the design of on-chip interconnect networks. Accurate characterization of signal propagation and crosstalk requires modeling skin effect inside lossy conductors, as well as electromagnetic coupling between conductors. Volume-based techniques such as the finite element method are computationally expensive at high frequencies, due to the need for an extremely fine mesh within conductors. Although surface integral equation methods reduce the dimensionality of the problem by requiring only a surface discretization of the conductors [1], simulating modern interconnect networks of increasing size and intricacy still poses a significant computational challenge.

articleTitle: Optimization Method in 2D DC Electric Field Cloaking and Shielding
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In order to design shielding or cloaking shells for manipulating DC electric fields we formulate and solve inverse problems of electrical conductivity. The shells consist of a finite number of layers filled with homogeneous isotropic medium. The design problems under study are reduced to control problems with the electrical conductivities of layers taken as controls. These problems are solved numerically using the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Results of numerical experiments obtained in this study describe easy-to-manufacture layered shells that have the high cloaking or shielding performance.

articleTitle: Stochastic FDTD versus correlated/non-correlated Monte Carlo
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This contribution presents a comparison of the stochastic FDTD [1] (S-FDTD) and Monte Carlo methods, for the analysis of thin-wire antennas with the Holland formulation [2]. An analysis is made on the effect of crosscorrelation between the variables affected by incertitude, and the variability of the observed quantities.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Number of Stochastic EM Sources with Partially Correlated Radiation in Far-Field Using Neural Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Neural model based on multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural networks, capable to determine the number of partially correlated stochastic radiation EM sources present in a monitoring spatial sector, is proposed in the paper. Stochastic radiation sources are moving in the azimuth plane along a line trajectory. Sources are mutually correlated with the same value of correlation level but this value can change during their movement. Also, sources can enter or leave the observed sector so that their number in the sector varies. Signals coming from the sources in the monitoring sector are sampled by a uniform linear antenna array and based on this sampling a spatial correlation matrix is created. The values of correlation matrix elements are used as an input to the proposed neural model that has to estimate the number of stochastic sources present in the observed sector. The neural model presented in this paper can determine a presence of maximum three stochastic sources in the 30° wide sector while the level of mutual correlation of sources can vary between 0.05 and 0.5.

Author Keywords: Estimation of the number of stochastic EM Sources

articleTitle: Gesture recognition using FMCW radar and machine learning on a Raspberry Pi platform
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We demonstrate how to implement a simple gesture recognition system based on a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system, powered by a commercial 24 GHz radar module controlled by a Raspberry Pi computer augmented by a cheap AD/DA card. The basic setup of the FMCW radar consists of an up-chirp and down-chirp pulse, where the I/Q-signals are recorded through the AD/DA card.

articleTitle: On the Techniques to Design 3D-Printable Arbitrarily Height-Modulated Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A novel modelling technique to design microwave 3D-printable filters based on arbitrarily height-modulated sub- strate integrated waveguides (SIW) is presented in this paper. In the literature, different topologies have been already employed to design filters based on SIW. Nevertheless, none of these solutions have analyzed the behavior of the modulation of the height of the filters. This is due to the difficulty of manufacturing the prototypes with conventional procedures. In this paper, the techniques to design and manufacture these filters, provided with microstrip transitions for their validation, are presented.

articleTitle: Improving Gain of a Broadband Antipodal Vivaldi Array fed by a Tapered Excitation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The application of a tapered excitation to the antenna elements of an array is recommended in order to reduce the height of the sidelobe in the far-field antenna pattern improving the link in the forward direction. To implement a specific excitation function, it is desirable to have a power divider in the frequency range of operation. Here, we present two designs: a) using a broadband equal power divider with a variable attenuator and b) unequal power divider. In both cases, the input excitations are reduced to limit the amplitude of the excitation at a particular port. We have selected three tapered functions: Chebyshev, Kaiser, and the zeroth order Prolate spheroidal wave function. For each tapered excitation, we calculate the spatial power distribution of the far-field H-plane pattern.

articleTitle: Spectral Projection Model for Analyzing Electromagnetic Scattering from Two Dimensional Conducting Objects
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel new formulation based on the addition theorem for Bessel and Hankel functions is developed for electromagnetic scattering from two-dimensional, conducting objects. The addition theorem is used to represent the Green's function as a projection of spectral signatures of source points on to spectral signatures of the observation points. The spectral signatures are defined in terms of the Bessel and Hankel functions. Known as the spectral projection model, this formulation allows one to define the scattered signal in terms of a spectral signature of a virtual image current as opposed to induced surface currents. The spectral signatures do not have to be defined in space and can easily be related to the scattered field in the far-field. MATLAB simulations of scattering from two-dimensional objects are used to verify and validate this new formulation. The model is applied to infinitely long conducting cylinders with elliptical cross-sections. The results from the spectral projection model are compared with those from the Method of Moments (MoM) for accuracy and speed. The results indicate that the new model performs well for cylinders with elliptical cross-sections for moderate axial ratios. For larger axial ratios, the model has to be modified to account for the wider spectral signatures. A new multi-reference spectral signature is defined and shown to work for scattering from cylinders with large axial ratios.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties Mapping via Segmented and Phaseless Contrast Source Inversion
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In-vivo estimation of electrical properties of biological tissues is relevant in several medical applications, ranging from hyperthermia treatment planning to dosimetry. In this contribution, we propose a novel inverse scattering approach addressing this problem. In particular, the approach is based on inverting phaseless B1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> measurements acquired in a magnetic resonance scanner. Moreover, it takes advantage of an innovative use of the segmented anatomy model derived by magnetic resonance images in order to regularize the inverse scattering problem.

articleTitle: Planar Phased Array Feed for the Lovell Telescope
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Phased Array Feed (PAF) is an emerging technology to increase the field of view for the radio telescopes based on reflector antennas. The Lovell Telescope has been used for over 50 years for investigating cosmic phenomena. This work reports a low profile circular PAF design for the Lovell antenna based on the experience from the antenna design for the Mid-Frequency Aperture Array of Square Kilometre Array. The objective is to provide a low profile and cost effective PAF design suitable for cryogenically cooling of the entire front-end to improve noise performance. The EM performance of the proposed PAF design and its characteristics are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Revisiting Phaseless Near-Field Antenna Measurements via Modelling Near-Field Measured Data in Full-Wave Solvers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: As emerging technologies move towards mmWave frequencies and beyond, a significant challenge faced by antenna engineers today is measuring the radiation characteristics of the antenna in a precise and cost-effective way. Amongst the various techniques developed, the near field measurement technique has gained special interest for high-frequency measurements due to its compactness and accuracy. Its compact nature reduces the need for extensive space, allowing for higher signal to noise ratios than those obtained from a conventional far-field chamber. Such near-field systems typically consist of an antenna under test (AUT) mounted on a pedestal, and a probe that captures the fields radiated by the AUT. A vector-network analyzer (VNA) typically records the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> data between the probe and the AUT, which is proportional to the near-field data transferred from the AUT to the probe. In general, to successfully characterize the antenna, both the amplitude and phase of the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> must be accurately recorded by the VNA. While the amplitude is relatively immune to minor errors that can arise during a measurement, the phase can be an extremely sensitive to these errors, making precise phase measurement a challenge. Further, for frequencies beyond mmWave, the availability of the vector instruments can get rather limited, and such instruments can be prohibitively expensive.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Impedance Cylindrical Metasurface for the Given Polarization Ellipse of Conformal Phased Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: The paper provides a solution to the 2D-problem of synthesizing the impedance tensor of a homogeneous circular cylindrical metasurface (MS) for any preassigned polarization ellipse of radiation from a conformal phased antenna array (PAA). A 2D-model of PAA near a cylindrical MS in the form of a circular lattice of longitudinal ribbons with currents is considered. The solution is subject to the additional requirement of the invariance of the PAA polarization with respect to the angles of observation of the field. It is shown that the ellipticity coefficient and the angle of inclination of the major axis of the polarization ellipse of the PAA are explicitly determined only by the impedance of the MS. The dependences of the impedance on the specified parameters of the PAA polarization ellipse are investigated. The class of realizable polarizations of PAA in the particular case of reciprocal MSs is established.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Analysis of Chirped Gaussian Pulse Propagation in a Metamaterial Medium
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: An asymptotic analysis of the unified, exact integral representation of the propagated field, is elaborated for the case of chirped Gaussian pulse propagation in a linear Lorentz-type metamaterial medium. The topography of the unified phase function and the dynamics of its saddle points are investigated and their ramifications in the application of the asymptotic methodology are elaborated.

articleTitle: How to split electric and toroidal dipole excitations due to superconductivity?
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)

articleTitle: Ideal Magnetic Dipole: Scattering and Mantle Cloaking Effects
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Artificial magnetic response is one of the recent research topics that is receiving significant attention. Nevertheless, because of the difficulties in exciting not only the magnetic moment but also multipoles of different order, and the presence of losses, the efficiency of its generation is strongly compromised. On the other hand, the presence of a cloaking phenomena can be described in terms of anapole mode, which consists in the compensation of the scattering due to the moment of the electric dipole with the toroidal one. Because of this effect, the remaining part of the field will exhibit a strong(er) magnetic dipole moment response. In the present study, the response of a cloaking device based on a real-life geometry is therefore analysed with particular focus on the anapole mode excitation and ideal magnetic dipole behavior.

articleTitle: Toward More Geometrically Adaptive Compression of Moment Matrices
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In recent years, fast direct integral equation solvers have been developed, as an alternative to iterative solver, for problems that suffer from ill-conditioning or when a solution is sought for many right-hand-sides. These solvers rely on the fast computation of a compressed representation of the impedance matrix. Then, the compressed representation's factorized (effectively `solved”) form is computed and applied to each right-hand-side. If the factorized form inherits the original matrix's compressibility, the savings in memory are maintained and the solution for each right-hand-side is, indeed, fast. The compression of the impedance matrix is often performed in a hierarchical manner. The geometry is first partitioned into clusters of basis and testing functions. Then, a hierarchical block structure for compression is defined, in accordance with the choice of hierarchical algebraic procedure for computing the compressed factorized form, e.g., [1], [2], or [3]. Matrix blocks, corresponding to interactions between sources and observers, that are assumed compressible, in some sense, are identified and compressed.

articleTitle: Wave-Particle Interactions in Earth's Inner Magnetosphere: Experimental Results from BARREL
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: In Earth's inner magnetosphere where the plasmasphere, ring current and radiation belts overlap, energy and momentum are exchanged between different plasma populations by plasma waves. Resonant interaction with these waves can lead to rapid loss of radiation belt and ring current electrons to the atmosphere, called precipitation. For example, electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) waves are thought to scatter ultra-relativistic electrons into the atmosphere on the duskside of the magnetosphere, while whistler-mode chorus causes rapid (~100ms) electron microbursts near dawn. Over the past six years, more than 50 BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Electron Losses) balloons have been launched, making observations of energetic (~20 keV - 10 MeV) electron precipitation in both hemispheres [Millan et al., 2013]. The combination of BARREL multi-point balloon measurements with in situ particle and wave measurements from equatorial spacecraft (e.g. Van Allen Probes, Arase, GOES) provides a unique opportunity to study the wave-particle interactions that cause precipitation. Moreover, BARREL and other low altitude measurements of precipitation (e.g., from POES, CSSWE, FIREBIRD, AC-6) can be used to determine the spatial scale of the region over which the wave-particle interactions occur.

articleTitle: A Study on Matrix Derivatives for the Sensitivity Analysis of Electromagnetic Eigenvalue Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Electromagnetic eigenvalue problems with varying design parameters appear in many application areas of numerical field simulations such as the tuning process of microwave filters. The sensitivity of the eigensolutions with respect to changes in geometric or material parameters is generally well understood if these changes are `small', and the numerical size of the formulation (the number of degrees of freedom) remains unchanged. In such cases the mapping from parameter changes to the detuning of eigenfrequencies can often be assumed as continuous, and the standard perturbation theory for algebraic eigenvalue problems (EVP) may be applied. E.g., the sensitivity of the eigenvalue of a single mode in a symmetric, generalized EVP is given by [1].

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling Of Erroneous Software Behavior In Embedded Digital Systems Due To Extreme Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Predicting the behavior of digital electronic and embedded systems subjected to extreme electromagnetic interference (EEMI) is a growing concern for military and civilian systems operating in ever denser ambient electromagnetic (EM) or Radio Frequency (RF) environments. While the interaction of the EM/RF stimulus with the system circuitry occurs at the physical or hardware level (“glitch”), the manifestation of this interaction is often observed as an erroneous behavior in the software state of the system under EM/RF stress. In this paper, we present ongoing progress in developing Markov State Vector Machine (MSVM) modeling frameworks for describing the software state of a microcontroller-based digital electronic system subjected to an externally applied glitch. We also describe our ongoing work in developing predictive MSVM models for the erroneous responses of complex software scripts when the underlying digital electronic system is subjected to EEMI glitches. Our predictive capability will help EMI/EMC engineers develop quick assessment tools for modeling the behavior of higher complexity digital electronic and embedded systems exposed to extreme electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: A Low Rank Study of Two Spatial Unknown Groups as a Function of Separation Distance
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a frequency domain MOM numerical study of a two-body problem where the rank, rank fraction (compressibility), SVD singular values and norm properties of the interaction matrix are examined as a function of body separation from 0.1 to 100 λ. Three practical real world two-body configurations were examined: two coplanar 4 ×4 λ plates, two spheres, ka=6.28 each, and two parallel 4 ×4 λ plates. Of particular interest is the numerical rank of the interaction and the rank fraction for a normalized error tolerance of ε=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> and at what separation distance can the Z12 interaction matrix be expressed as an Rk low rank outer product UV form. The results show that even at 0.1 λ, Z12 can be well approximated in Rk form for the co-planar and sphere cases. In the parallel 4 λ plate configuration, an Rk representation can be utilized for separations greater than about 0.4 λ. These results are far less restrictive than the admissibility criteria suggested in the hierarchical methodology.

articleTitle: Imaging in the presence of direction-dependent effects with the MeerKAT radio telescope
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: We discuss how the resulting gain solutions can be associated with remaining unmodelled effects, and how deconvolution of extended emission can be improved.

articleTitle: An Eigenfunction Expansion Method for the Analysis of the Source-Excited Fields in a Magnetoplasma
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: Excitation of electromagnetic waves by sources immersed in a homogeneous magnetoplasma is studied using an eigenfunction expansion method. The total field is sought in terms of vector modal solutions of the source-free Maxwell equations. The content of the modal spectrum is determined and the eigenmodes of the homogeneous magnetoplasma are found to form a continuous set. The source-excited field is represented by an integral expansion in terms of the obtained continuous-spectrum modes and the expansion coefficients of such a field representation are derived in explicit form using the mode orthogonality relation. The developed approach is applied to the analysis of radiation from a rotating magnetic-field source in the whistler frequency range.

articleTitle: A Novel Vertical Patch Antenna for Pattern Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A novel vertical patch antenna (VPA) for pattern reconfiguration is proposed. It consists of a VPA and a monopole antenna, which can operate independently. Simulation and experimental results show that the radiation patterns can be easily steered between omnidirectional pattern of 18% bandwidths and bidirectional pattern of 17.8% bandwidths. The whole radiation pattern can cover a beam range of 0~90° in elevation angle with the gain greater than 0dB.

articleTitle: On the Practical Effectiveness of the Nonredundant Spherical NF-FF Transformation for Offset Mounted Long AUTs
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Electromagnetics in Advanced Applications (ICEAA)
abstract: A laboratory assessment of a recently proposed spherical near-field to far-field (NF-FF) transformation technique for a long antenna under test (AUT) mounted in offset configuration, which requires an amount of NF measurements minimum and equal to that needed for the onset mounting, is provided in this work. The interest for this technique is due to the fact that sometimes, for practical limitations, it can be impossible an onset mounting, where the AUT center and the scanning sphere one coincide.
